Alger, 6 novembre 2026 (Algeria Tech) —: Algiers, November 6, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Höttges stated on Thursday that SpaceX's Starlink Mobile project will require an investment of at least $200 billion to become a major player in the United States. He compared this challenge to the disruption seen in the automotive industry with Tesla.
Deutsche Telekom remet en question le co: Deutsche Telekom questions the cost of Starlink Mobile
Lors d'un appel de résultats jeudi, le P: During an earnings call on Thursday, Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Höttges expressed reservations about SpaceX's ability to transform Starlink Mobile into a major operator in the United States. He estimated that Elon Musk's project would require a minimum investment of $200 billion.
Höttges a pointé que SpaceX a acquis 76: Höttges pointed out that SpaceX has acquired 76 MHz of spectrum, compared to 400 MHz for Deutsche Telekom. To achieve a competitive position, hundreds of billions of dollars would be needed, according to his calculations. Furthermore, building a network would require $20 to $30 billion for towers, considering that Deutsche Telekom owns 85,000 towers.
SpaceX a présenté Starlink Mobile comme: SpaceX has presented Starlink Mobile as a direct competitor to T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon, using satellites and a terrestrial network. Reports mention the use of 80,000 towers and discussions to acquire Boost Mobile. Qualcomm has announced technological support for the project.
Höttges reconnaît la menace potentielle,: Höttges acknowledges the potential threat, noting that Musk has chips, data centers, AI, and satellites. He could integrate social services or AI agents, creating a new form of communication. However, he insists that this is not an easy feat, recalling Tesla's impact on the automotive industry.
